entries.reason: Provenance record of the public-domain NASA interview excerpt (#308). The 64-hex runs are the SHA-256 digests of the source MP3 and of the cut excerpt, which pin the fixture bytes; they are content addresses, not device tokens.

SHA-256 content digests of media assets (spec 13.3A). They are 64 hex characters, the same shape as a PLAUD legacy static device token, but they are derived from file bytes and are not credentials. Keeping them readable is what makes a deduplication bug diagnosable.

Content-addressed media archive paths (spec 13.4) of the form media/sha256/<first-two>/<digest-prefix>.m4a. The hex run is a content digest prefix used as a storage path, not a device token; this corpus is the path-guard hostile-filename fixture and contains no credentials.

Update manifest fixtures (spec 20.3). The 64-hex runs are the `package_sha256` and `manifest_sha256` digests the updater verifies, computed over the fixture packages in this directory; the manifests' only credential-shaped field is the detached Ed25519 signature, which is base64 and not a secret in any case (the private half lives nowhere in the tree).

Recording-archive fixtures (spec 13.4) are binary containers. Their uncompressed manifest records carry the SHA-256 digest of every member, and the deflate payload after them is arbitrary bytes that occasionally spell a hex run of the same length. Neither is a credential: these fixtures are generated by the archive writer from synthetic recordings, which hold no tokens.
Extraction-evaluation corpus (spec 19.2). Each item's `media.sha256` is the content digest that pins the sample bytes the evaluation runs against — a content address, not a device token.

The diarization harness plan's `session_id` is the name of a scripted synthetic session (`scripted-session-01`), matched because the generic credential-parameter pattern treats any `session_id` as a session token. There is no authentication anywhere in the speaker evaluation: it reads local fixtures only.

The ADR-0400 condition-4 session timelines name each synthetic session (`librispeech-session-01`..`-03`), and the generic credential-parameter pattern treats any `session_id` as a session token. Same fact as the harness plan above: the speaker evaluation authenticates against nothing, it lays out local LibriSpeech clips from a fixed seed.
The LibriSpeech plan carries the same `session_id` names as the session timelines it shares a run with; see the entry above.

Each utterance's `media_sha256` is the content digest that pins the clip bytes the EER run reads — a content address of a file in the corpus, the same shape and the same non-secret as `**/fixtures/eval/corpus.yaml` above.
